Elliot Chen: quick check — customer asked in SOC2 questionnaire: "Are request logs redacted for PII before storing? Who can access raw logs/KMS keys? any subprocessors with access?" Need a one-liner we can paste back.

Priya Kapoor: Short answer: we redact user-facing PII at ingest, store request metadata. Raw full payloads are only retained for 7 days and accessible by SRE + Security with approvals. See: https://redwood.internal/security/logging-policy

Tim O'Leary: Clarifying: we have two streams:
- `ingest-scrubbed` (default, PII redacted)
- `raw-debug` (only for active incidents, TTL 7 days)

In prod config: `LOG_PII_REDACTION=true` and the scrubber uses regex + NER-based filters.

Jorge Rivera: For subprocessors: none of our infra subprocessors get raw logs unless explicit approval. Access path: create a ticket in #sec-requests (e.g. SR-472), include justification, and get Security + Legal signoff. KMS key grants are scoped to service principals and timeboxed.

Priya Kapoor: Pasteable wording: "We apply automated PII redaction at ingestion; raw payload access is restricted to SRE, Platform, and Security and requires formal approval (ticket SR-###) and is time-limited. KMS keys used to encrypt logs are customer-managed keys or service CMKs and access is audited; subprocessors do not receive key access without an approved contract and scoped grant."

Elliot Chen: awesome — can someone add SR-472 as an example? I'll paste.

SecurityBot: Document updated: https://redwood.internal/security/logging-policy (v2.1) :lock:

Tim O'Leary: one nit: change "SRE and Security" -> "SRE, Platform, and Security" — Platform ops sometimes need temporary access for debugging (with approval).

Priya Kapoor: ack. final pasteable: "We apply automated PII redaction at ingestion; raw payload access is restricted to SRE, Platform, and Security and requires formal approval (ticket SR-472) and is time-limited. KMS keys used to encrypt logs are CMKs and access is audited; subprocessors do not get key access without an approved contract & scoped grant."

Elliot Chen: pasted back to customer, they replied "thanks — can you confirm which subprocessors?" — @Jorge Rivera is Legal the right owner?

Jorge Rivera: Legal holds the contracts list; Security maintains access exceptions and the current subprocessors CSV. I'll attach the CSV in the approval ticket and link here.

Priya Kapoor: +1. If they ask about encryption in transit/at rest — say: "All logs are encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest with CMKs; key access is audited and limited to Security & Platform ops with just-in-time grants."

Elliot Chen: perfect, thanks all :thumbsup:
